newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia sees $2.57 bln foreign investment in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sees $2.57 bln foreign investment in 1997.

text.p: BOGOTA, May 2 Reuter - Colombia will see a $2.57 billion inflow of new direct foreign investment in 1997, the central bank said in a report Friday.
Including 1997 estimates, it forecast that more than $10.3 billion of new direct foreign investment would flow into Colombia by the year 2000.

In its report, the central bank forecast the oil sector would attract $1.1 billion in new foreign investment this year and draw an average $600 million annual foreign investment between now and the year 2000.
The bank forecast that the sale of the state-run coal company Carbocol's stake in the giant Cerrejon Zona Norte mine would net $600 million for the nation.
Carbocol has a 50 percent stake in the mine, which produces 13 million tonnes of coal annually and is operated by a subsidiary of the Exxon Corp. The sell-off is due sometime in 1998.
